# pve_user_token (Data Source)

Reads API tokens of a PVE user (`GET /access/users/{userid}/token[/{tokenid}]`). Set `tokenid` to read a single token's settings; omit it to list every token of the user. The token secret is never returned by reads, so `token_value` is exclusive to the `pve_user_token` resource at create time.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.

# List every API token of a PVE user.
data "pve_user_token" "root_tokens" {
  userid = "root@pam"
}

# Or read one token's settings.
data "pve_user_token" "ci" {
  userid  = "root@pam"
  tokenid = "ci"
}

output "ci_token_privsep" {
  value = data.pve_user_token.ci.privsep
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `userid` (String) Full User ID in `name@realm` format whose tokens to read, e.g. `root@pam`.

### Optional

- `tokenid` (String) Token identifier to read a single token. Omit to list all tokens in `tokens` instead.

### Read-Only

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment of the token (single mode only).
- `expire` (Number) API token expiration date (seconds since epoch). `0` means no expiration date; null inherits the user's expiry (single mode only).
- `id` (String) `<userid>!<tokenid>` in single mode, `<userid>` in list mode.
- `privsep` (Boolean) Whether the token's privileges are restricted with separate ACLs (single mode only).
- `tokens` (Attributes List) The user's tokens (list mode only, when `tokenid` is omitted). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tokens))

Read-Only:

- `tokenid` (String) Token identifier.
